description:
FOUND s490 (Fable), by the #1860 review probes run against main ab4da8b4 BEFORE
the agent report (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s490/probes/p1860.pl scenario 3 pass 1 and
4e pass 1; isolated by ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s490/probes/p-firstrun.pl).

SHAPE.  prog.pl -> `use A3;` ; lib/A3.pm -> `use B2; sub go { return zap + 1 }` ;
lib/B2.pm exports `sub zap () {...}` (an EMPTY PROTOTYPE, a parse fact: with it
`zap + 1` is zap()+1 = 8, without it zap(+1) = 107).  `pcl -I lib prog.pl`:

  mode, FRESH cache dir                 perl   pcl    A3 manifest
  default (script cache, fasl build)      8    *107*  missing mod B2
  --no-cache                              8      8    (none)
  PCL_NO_FASL_CACHE=1 (text path)         8      8    dep mod B2
  default, SECOND run, same cache         8      8    dep mod B2   (self-heals: #1284
                                                      missing re-check re-transpiles A3)

So the FIRST run of any script whose modules have their own dependencies on the
-I / PERL5LIB path is transpiled with those dependencies UNRESOLVED -- every
parse fact they carry (block-arg prototypes, empty prototypes, exported names)
is silently absent -- and the answer is right from the second run on.  Pre-#1841
`pcl` was right on every run (the script was `load`ed as text AFTER its preamble
had set @INC).  A new REGRESSION of the default-on script cache, first-run only,
SILENT.

MECHANISM (read from cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, p-run-script-cached docstring +
%p-transpile-inc-args).  On a MISS the script text is compile-file'd, and the
program's `use` statements run at COMPILE-FILE time -- before the entry's own
preamble has set @INC.  s488b knew the RESOLVER needs a search path there and
seeded *p-core-inc-dirs* (SEED-INC-DIRS), which p-find-module-in-inc falls back
to -- so A3 itself IS found.  But A3's transpile gets its `-I` list from
%p-transpile-inc-args, which reads @INC ONLY -- still empty (or holding only a
`use lib` dir already executed) -- so the child pl2cl resolves nothing of A3's
under the program's -I list.  #1284's "ONE SEARCH PATH" rule is broken exactly
where the resolver has a fallback the transpile list lacks.

FIX SHAPE (RULED, Fable s490): ONE list builder.  p-find-module-in-inc's walk
(@INC entries, then the *p-core-inc-dirs* / runtime-lib fallback) becomes a
helper, and BOTH p-find-module-in-inc and %p-transpile-inc-args iterate it (the
latter still dropping the shim dir and non-string entries) -- so the two cannot
diverge again; #1860's R2 clause uses the same helper for its "current walk".
NOT a special case keyed on "@INC is empty": a script with `use lib "x"; use A3;`
has @INC = (x) at that moment and the same hole.  Appending the fallback dirs in
normal operation only repeats directories the child perl already searches, later
in the same order (first-match unchanged) -- VERIFY by the second-run
re-transpile count and the sweep, not by argument.

GUARD: Pl/t/script-cache-01.t -- the table above as rows on a FRESH
PCL_CACHE_DIR: first run 8 AND A3's manifest carries `dep mod B2`, never
`missing`; plus the `use lib` variant.  Inverse-verify on ab4da8b4 (first-run row
FAILS there).

WHY s488b's GUARDS MISSED IT: they tested script -> B directly (the script's own
transpile is handed inc-dirs explicitly); the hole needs script -> A -> B on a
cold cache, and it heals before a second look.

Related: #1841 (the script cache), #1284 (one search path), #1860 (R2 uses the
same walk), s488b records.  Assigned to s490a as member 0 (s490).

=== DONE (s490a, 2026-09-18, member 0) ===

FIXED exactly as ruled: ONE list builder.  `%p-inc-search-dirs` returns
@INC-as-a-list followed by the FALLBACK (`*p-core-inc-dirs*`, or PCL's lib/
beside the runtime when no preamble ever ran), and BOTH `p-find-module-in-inc`
and `%p-transpile-inc-args` iterate it.  A first match over the concatenation
is exactly the two-stage search `p-find-module-in-inc` was written as, so the
resolver is unchanged by construction; `%p-transpile-inc-args` still drops the
shim dir and non-string entries, and now DEDUPES by string (in ordinary
operation the fallback repeats @INC, and a first match does not care but a
command line does).  Not keyed on "@INC is empty" â the `use lib "x"` variant
was probed and reproduced on the base (107 / `missing:ULDep`) and is fixed.

MEASURED (the reproducers, PCL_TREE-parameterised, kept in the s490a worktree
at scratch/s490a/probes/):
  * p-firstrun.pl (Fable's): base `default  perl=8 pcl=107  missing:B2`
    -> tree `default  perl=8 pcl=8  dep:B2`, all four modes 8.
  * p-uselib.pl (the `use lib` variant, this session): base `perl=8 pcl=107
    missing:ULDep` -> tree `perl=8 pcl=8  dep:ULDep`.
  * p1860.pl scenario 3 pass 1 and 4e pass 1 â the two rows this bug owned â
    became `same` (scratch/s490a/probes/p1860-member0.out).
  * THE APPEND IS INERT IN ORDINARY OPERATION, measured rather than argued:
    nine `pcl` runs (hello / Carp / JSON::PP / Moo / List::Util+File::Spec+
    POSIX / a -I module chain / a `use lib` chain / evals / cl/pack-impl.pl)
    against ONE fresh cache, run twice, counting entries the second run
    REPLACED (by INODE: an entry is published temp+rename, a last-use stamp is
    not).  base+member-0: 0 of 50 modules / 18 scripts / 178 evals.  RAW
    ab4da8b4, same harness: 2 rewritten AND two answers that MOVE between run
    1 and run 2 (chain 7->8, uselib 12->13) â that is the size of this bug.
  * Full gate, full perl-tests sweep and the @INC-touching companion files: in
    the batch's final bars (s490a commit 6d951d2a and the session record).

GUARD: six rows in Pl/t/script-cache-01.t (51 -> 57), first run AND the
manifest (`dep:FRDep` / `dep:ULDep`, never `missing:`), plus the `use lib`
variant.  Inverse-verified on a `git archive ab4da8b4` extraction: four of the
six FAIL there.  File wall time 12 s -> 16.2 s (`prove --timer`), well under
module-fasl-cache-01.t's 25.6 s.
subject: SILENT WRONG, FIRST RUN ONLY (regression of the default-on script cache #1841): on a script-cache MISS the program's `use` runs at compile-file time before the preamble sets @INC, and %p-transpile-inc-args reads @INC only -- so every MODULE the script loads is transpiled WITHOUT the -I list and its own dependencies' prototypes/exports are silently missing (perl 8, pcl 107 on run 1; 8 from run 2 on)
